beurre.note: In cakes, for a lighter version.

oeufs.note: About 60 g of applesauce per egg, in cakes.
1 tbsp ground + 3 tbsp water per egg, let sit for 5 min to thicken.

lait.note: Good substitute for both cooking and drinking.

crème fraîche épaisse.note: For a dairy-free version, adds a slight coconut flavor.

farine.note: To thicken a sauce; does not replace flour for making a cake rise.
Changes the texture and taste, denser and richer.

sucre.note: Slightly reduce the recipe's liquid quantity (honey is moist).
More pronounced taste, slightly reduce the recipe's liquid.

levure chimique.note: Combine with an acidic ingredient (vinegar, lemon juice) for it to work.

vin blanc.note: Add a little lemon juice to bring back the wine's acidity.

vin rouge.note: Add a little balsamic vinegar for acidity and color.

huile d'olive.note: Good source of omega-3, neutral taste.

yaourt nature.note: A bit denser, slightly less tangy.
Richer, use in a slightly smaller amount.

parmesan.note: For a vegan version, brings a similar umami taste.

moutarde.note: Combine with a little vinegar to bring back the acidity.

ail.note: About 1/8 tsp per fresh garlic clove.

oignon.note: Use the white part, more delicate taste.

citron.note: For acidity only, without the citrus flavor.

vinaigre balsamique.note: Add a pinch of sugar to bring back the slightly sweet side.

cube de bouillon.note: Diluted in water, adds salty umami flavor.

crème liquide entière.note: A bit less rich, but a similar texture.

mascarpone.note: Mix with a little thick crème fraîche for richness.

chocolat noir.note: Mix with butter and sugar to get a similar texture.

riz.note: Higher in protein, slightly different texture.

pâtes.note: For a gluten-free version, quicker cooking.

sucre vanillé.note: A few drops are enough, add to regular sugar.

miel.note: Add a bit more liquid to compensate (honey is moist).

sauce soja.note: For a gluten-free version, very similar taste.
Diluted in a little water; the umami flavor will be less present.
